instructions.content: Group commits by what kind of thing changed (infrastructure, application logic, tests, housekeeping), not by when they were written or which ticket they belong to.
Present the proposed grouping as a table and wait for explicit user approval before creating any branches or cherry-picking.
NEVER name branches with sequence numbers (wave-1, phase-2, part-1) -- sequence names lose meaning after any rebase or reorder, and a reviewer cannot determine scope without reading the full diff.

NEVER create branches or cherry-pick before the user approves the grouping -- grouping requires domain knowledge the agent does not have, and a misassigned commit means deleting and recreating branches.
NEVER split commits that share a single failing test / broken intermediate state -- if PR 1 removes a handler and PR 2 adds its replacement, PR 1 alone fails CI and the merge queue blocks.
NEVER write MR descriptions as file lists or commit logs -- a reviewer can already read the diff; use the What/Why format instead.

NEVER leave cherry-pick conflicts unresolved before reporting completion -- always resolve every conflict and verify the branch actually builds (not just that cherry-pick exited 0) before reporting success.
Stack each subsequent PR's branch on the previous PR's branch (PR 1 targets base, PR 2 targets PR 1, etc.) and use cherry-pick to distribute the approved commits into each branch in order.
After creating branches, remind the user which target branch each MR must be opened against, and that they must be merged in stack order.

Adapt concern labels to the codebase -- collapse to two groups (application logic + tests) when there is no infrastructure layer, or use the codebase's own taxonomy (frontend/backend/data) if that fits better.

Do not decompose when the branch has only 2-4 commits touching the same component, when all files are tests for one feature, when the work is already in review, or when commits are tightly coupled such that cherry-pick reordering would break intermediate branches.
Use this skill when the user says a PR is too big, asks to split a PR, wants to decompose a branch, or needs to break work into reviewable chunks.
